title: What training do assisted living facility administrators and staff need in Florida?
seoTitle: Florida ALF core and staff training
description: Florida ALF training under s. 429.52 and Rule 59A-36.011: 26-hour core training and test, 2-hour preservice orientation, dementia and medication hours.
shortAnswer: In Florida, an assisted living facility administrator or manager must complete at least 26 hours of core training and pass a competency test with 75 percent within 3 months, then 12 hours of continuing education every 2 years. New staff need a 2-hour preservice orientation before interacting with residents, then in-service training within 30 days, a 1-hour state dementia course, and topic-specific hours under section 429.52, Florida Statutes, and Rule 59A-36.011.
keyTakeaways: Core training for administrators and managers is at least 26 hours plus a competency test with a minimum passing score of 75 percent, completed within 3 months of taking the role.

Every new employee who has not completed core training needs a preservice orientation of at least 2 hours before interacting with residents, covering residents' rights and the facility's license type and services.

Direct care staff need in-service training on infection control before giving personal care, and on adverse incidents, emergency procedures, residents' rights, abuse reporting, resident behavior and activities of daily living within 30 days.
Under section 430.5025, staff with resident contact complete a 1-hour Department of Elder Affairs dementia course within 30 days, and personal care staff complete 3 more hours within 7 months.
Unlicensed staff who assist with self-administered medication need 6 hours from a registered nurse or licensed pharmacist before starting, then 2 hours every year.
regulator: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA), with the Florida Department of Elder Affairs
appliesTo: Assisted living facilities licensed under Part I of Chapter 429, Florida Statutes
ALF administrators and managers, and extended congregate care (ECC) supervisors
All ALF employees, with additional hours for direct care staff, food service staff and staff assisting with medication
Registered core trainers and other training providers

sections.heading: Which laws set Florida ALF training requirements?

blocks.text: Two statutes and one rule. [Section 429.52, Florida Statutes](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/429.52), sets the core training, preservice orientation, continuing education and medication training framework. [Section 430.5025](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/430.5025), the Alzheimer's Disease and Related Forms of Dementia Education and Training Act, sets dementia training across covered providers including assisted living facilities. [Rule 59A-36.011, Florida Administrative Code](https://www.flrules.org/gateway/ruleNo.asp?id=59A-36.011), adds the hours, topics and documentation.

The rule was last amended effective June 5, 2024, to align with section 430.5025 as amended by chapter 2023-278, Laws of Florida. This page reflects the 2026 Florida Statutes and the rule as at November 2026.

sections.heading: What is ALF core training, and who must complete it?

blocks.text: Core training is the qualifying course and competency test for people who run an assisted living facility. Rule 59A-36.011(1) sets it at a minimum of 26 hours plus a competency test, with a minimum passing score of 75 percent and a test fee of no more than $200 each attempt.

items: Administrators and managers must complete core training, including passing the test, within 3 months of becoming an administrator or manager. Section 429.52(4) frames the administrator deadline as 90 days after employment and makes failure a violation subject to an administrative fine.
Administrators licensed as nursing home administrators under Part II of Chapter 468 are exempt.

The competency test must cover at least Florida ALF law and rules; residents' rights and reporting abuse, neglect and exploitation; special needs of elderly people and people with mental illness or developmental disabilities; nutrition and food service; medication management; firesafety and emergency procedures; and care of persons with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders.

Administrators and managers then need 12 hours of continuing education every 2 years under 429.52(5). Anyone who lets continuing education lapse is treated as new and must retake core training and pass the test again.

blocks.text: Core training must be delivered by trainers registered with AHCA. Under 429.52(11), a core trainer generally needs either a 4-year degree plus 3 years in ALF management after core certification, or 5 years in ALF management plus 1 year of teaching experience, or prior employment as a core trainer for the agency or department.

sections.heading: What must new ALF staff complete before and after starting work?

blocks.text: A preservice orientation before any resident contact, then in-service training within 30 days. Under 429.52(1)(a) and Rule 59A-36.011(2), the orientation is at least 2 hours, must cover residents' rights and the facility's license type and services, and must be documented by a statement signed by the employee and the administrator and kept in the personnel record.

blocks.text: Rule 59A-36.011(4) also requires a one-time HIV and AIDS education course within 30 days for employees not covered by section 456.033, and 59A-36.011(5) requires a staff member with current first aid and CPR certification to be in the facility at all times. For staging these deadlines, see [how to structure onboarding for regulated roles](/guides/how-to-structure-onboarding-for-regulated-roles).

sections.heading: What dementia training do Florida ALF staff need?

blocks.text: Everyone gets basic information at hire, and hours scale with contact. Under section 430.5025(4):

items: Upon beginning employment, each employee receives basic written information about interacting with persons with Alzheimer's disease or related dementia.

Within 30 days, each employee who provides personal care or has regular contact with residents completes a 1-hour training program provided online at no cost by the Department of Elder Affairs. It may count toward the 2-hour preservice orientation if completed before resident contact.

Within 7 months, each ALF employee who provides personal care completes 3 more hours covering behavior management, independence in activities of daily living, working with families, activities, environment and ethical issues.

In a facility that advertises and provides specialized Alzheimer's care, the 3 hours are due within 3 months for staff with personal care or regular contact, a further 4 hours of dementia-specific training is due within 6 months for personal care staff, and personal care staff then need at least 4 hours of continuing education each calendar year.

blocks.text: The annual continuing education may be delivered as on-the-job coaching by the administrator or a designee, documented in increments as small as a quarter hour, and must cover at least one dementia topic the employee was not trained on in the previous calendar year. A completed 1-hour course does not need to be repeated when an employee moves to another covered provider.

sections.heading: What additional training applies to medication assistance and specialty licenses?

blocks.text: Medication assistance has the most prescriptive rule. Under 429.52(6) and Rule 59A-36.011(6), unlicensed staff must complete at least 6 hours of training from a registered nurse or licensed pharmacist before assisting with self-administration of medication, and must demonstrate in person, physically and verbally, skills from reading a prescription label to using a glucometer and assisting with nebulizers and prefilled insulin pens. Two hours of continuing education are required every year, and may be online.

items: Food service: the administrator or food service designee needs at least 2 hours of continuing education each year in nutrition and food service, under 59A-36.011(7).

Extended congregate care: the administrator and ECC supervisor need core training plus 4 hours of initial ECC training, then 4 hours of continuing education every 2 years; direct care staff in ECC need at least 2 hours of in-service within 6 months.

Limited mental health: administrators, managers and staff with direct contact with mental health residents need 6 hours of specialized training within 6 months, then 3 hours of continuing education every 2 years.

sections.heading: What records does AHCA expect for ALF training?

blocks.text: Rule 59A-36.011(12) requires certificates for required training in personnel files, showing the program title, subject matter, agenda, hours, the trainee's name, dates and location, and the trainer's name, dated signature, credentials and license number where applicable. AHCA and the Department of Elder Affairs may attend and monitor in-service training. The table below is an illustrative register.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each Florida requirement to a role, a deadline measured from hire or role start, and the certificate fields Rule 59A-36.011(12) demands, so gaps show up before a survey. Dementia hours are tracked against the facility's specialized care status, since that changes the deadlines. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: How long does a new Florida ALF administrator have to finish core training?
faqs.a: Rule 59A-36.011(1)(b) requires administrators and managers to complete core training, including passing the competency test, within 3 months of becoming an administrator or manager. Section 429.52(4) expresses the administrator deadline as within 90 days after the date of employment as an administrator.

faqs.q: Can the state's 1-hour dementia course count toward preservice orientation?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 429.52(1)(c) provides that if an employee completes the 1-hour training required under section 430.5025 before interacting with residents, it may count toward the 2 hours of preservice orientation.

faqs.q: Do nurses and CNAs need the Florida ALF in-service training?
faqs.a: Some topics exempt them. The infection control hour and the 3 hours on resident behavior and activities of daily living in Rule 59A-36.011(3) exclude nurses, certified nursing assistants and home health aides trained under Rule 59A-8.0095. Other topics, such as adverse incident reporting and elopement response, apply to all direct care staff.

faqs.q: Is medication assistance training for Florida ALF staff a one-time requirement?
faqs.a: No. After the initial 6 hours from a registered nurse or licensed pharmacist, unlicensed staff must complete at least 2 hours of continuing education every year on assisting with self-administered medications and safe medication practices, which may be provided online.
